modules.description: Hardware is a signer, not magic. Backups must survive a fire, a theft, and a funeral without putting words in a group chat.

lessons.title: Hardware wallets, without worship
lessons.content:
# Hardware wallets, without worship

A hardware wallet keeps the seed in a small computer. The laptop proposes a transaction. The device signs if you confirm on **its** screen.

Ledger and Trezor are **examples of hardware wallets**, not ads, not a required purchase for Basic, not a halo. By the end of this lesson you should know what the box fixes, what it does not fix, and how people still empty a hardware wallet with their own finger.

## What it fixes

Malware that tries to export keys from Chrome does not find the seed on the laptop if the seed never lived there. A stolen laptop that does not also have the device and PIN is a brick, not a vault. A phishing site that asks you to type 12 words into a browser is easier to refuse when the words never appear on that browser.

That is the job: **the secret is not on the daily driver.** The daily driver still proposes. You still decide.

## What it does not fix

You confirm a swapped address because you did not read the device screen. You bought a used device that already had a seed. You typed the seed into a computer “to check.” You signed an unlimited approve. You stored the paper backup in Google Photos. You left every coin on an exchange and called the unopened box “self-custody.”

Hardware is a signer. It is not a babysitter. It is not an insurance policy. It is not colder than a paper you photographed.

**Buy from the manufacturer.** A marketplace “new Ledger, 40% off, seed already in the box” is a loaded vault. Initialize the device yourself. If a seed card came pre-written, the device is a gift for the seller.

TABLE
Do | Don't | Why
Initialize the device yourself | Use a pre-written seed from the box | The seller kept a copy
Confirm address on the device screen | Trust only the laptop monitor | Malware swaps the monitor
Keep a paper or steel backup | Photograph the seed “so I don’t lose the device” | The photo is the hotter copy
Buy from the maker | Buy a “discount sealed” unit from a random listing | Tamper and pre-load risk
Use it for amounts you would miss | Think it makes Approve unlimited safe | You still signed the gun
ENDTABLE

**Worked scenario.** The laptop shows your friend’s address. The hardware screen shows a different 0x.

1. That is the malware fight the device is for. If you click OK without reading the device, you brought a vault to a phishing site and opened it.
2. You reject on the device. You do not type the seed into the laptop “to see which address is real.”
3. You confirm the friend’s address from their receive screen, out of band, then try again.
4. If you had bought a pre-initialized device, both screens could be theatre: the seller already had the combination.
5. You can finish Basic without buying hardware. If you cannot keep a paper seed safe, hardware will not magically create discipline.

DIAGRAM
Laptop / phone  --proposes tx-->  Hardware device
                                      |
                                      v
                               You read ITS screen
                                      |
                    +-----------------+-----------------+
                    |                                   |
                 matches friend                    does not match
                    |                                   |
                    v                                   v
                 confirm                             reject
                    |
                    v
              signature leaves the box
              seed never sat in Chrome

Pre-filled seed in the box = seller already has a copy of this diagram.
ENDDIAGRAM

## Companion apps are still apps

The phone or desktop app that talks to the device can be cloned. Install from the official source. A clone companion will ask you to “enter seed to pair.” Real pairing does not need you to type the vault combination into a new pretty window.

Firmware updates come from the maker’s instructions, not from a Telegram file. A random firmware is a way to replace the small computer with a traitor.

You still need a paper or steel backup of the seed the device generated. The box can break, drown, or get lost. The backup is the combination. The box is a signer. Two objects. Module 1’s four objects still apply: the companion is the app, the device PIN is furniture, the seed is the vault, the chain is the book.

NOTE
You can finish Basic without buying hardware. If you cannot keep a paper seed safe, hardware will not magically create discipline. This academy will not sell you a device, will not ask you to “pair hardware for graduation,” and will not send a firmware file in a chat.
ENDNOTE


## When Basic is enough without a box

If your practice amount is smaller than the cost of the device, paper plus official app is the lab. Buy hardware later because the pile grew, not because a video said you are not a real holder. Worship is how people skip the paper backup and then lose the box.

## What this lesson is for

You can place hardware on the map without worship. Next: a backup drill for real life — prove the paper, then put it where fire, theft, and panic cannot all win at once.

## Say this out loud

- Hardware signs offline; you must still read its screen. The laptop can lie. The device screen is the destination.
- Never accept a pre-filled seed. Buy from the maker. Initialize yourself.
- Hardware does not fix bad approvals, photographed backups, or coins left on an exchange.
- Companion apps can be cloned. Pairing does not require typing 12 words into a website.
- Official shop, self-init, paper backup, read the device. Optional for this course.

Next: a backup drill for real life.

lessons.title: A backup drill for real life
lessons.content:
# A backup drill for real life

Keys outlive phones. They also outlive people. This is uncomfortable and it is part of self-custody.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to run a drill with zero or tiny funds: write, restore, receive a test, put the paper where you decided, and tell yourself one human plan.

## The drill (do with zero or tiny funds)

1. Create a wallet on an official app or on a hardware device you initialized. Write the words, numbered, no photo.
2. Confirm the in-app quiz of the word order.
3. Receive a tiny amount on the right network — BNB on BNB Smart Chain is enough to prove the door. Practice amount you can lose.
4. Restore on a second view **or** (carefully) on a spare profile or spare device you trust — not on a café PC, not on a cousin’s phone.
5. See the tiny amount. You have proved the backup. If you cannot restore, you do not have a backup. You have a rumour.
6. Put the paper where you decided. Tell **one** plan to yourself: who should be able to find this if you are in hospital.

If you cannot complete that drill, you are not ready to store an amount you would miss. That is not an insult. It is a measurement. Exchanges exist. IOUs exist. Self-custody is optional. Pretend self-custody is not.

A second profile on a phone can work as a restore test if the app supports it and you understand you are typing the seed on the same daily driver. A spare old phone that is offline is cleaner. A café PC is not a test. It is a leak.

TABLE
Drill step | Pass | Fail
Write numbered words | Paper matches the screen, read back once | Photo “to be sure,” chat copy
In-app confirmation | You tap the order from paper | You skip because it was slow
Tiny receive | Explorer shows it on your address | You funded rent first
Restore | Second view shows the same address and the tiny amount | You never tried, or you tried on a stranger’s laptop
Storage | Two boring places, not the phone bag | WhatsApp group, email, mattress only
Human plan | One sentence you could tell a lawyer or a trusted person | “They will figure it out”
ENDTABLE

**Worked scenario.** Jordan writes twelve words, skips restore, deposits a month of freelance pay, then drops the paper in a moving box that goes to another city.

1. The phone dies. He has a PIN. He has an email. He has no combination in reach.
2. A helper offers to recover from IMEI. That is nonsense for a seed. A second helper wants leftover funds to “trace.” That is theft.
3. The drill would have caught this at step 4 with a tiny amount, or at step 6 when he noticed the only copy was travelling with the furniture.
4. He can still be fine if the box arrives. Hope is not a control. Two locations exist so that one moving box is not the vault.
5. After this course he runs the drill on a new wallet before any amount that would annoy him. He does not “upgrade” the old rumour with a photo.

DIAGRAM
Practice amount
   --> drill restore
      --> paper in two boring places
         --> written plan for a human you trust
            --> only then: amount you would miss

Skip any arrow, and you have folklore, not a backup.
ENDDIAGRAM

## Two locations, one combination

Two copies of the same ordered list, not two different encodings. Fire in one house should not take both. Theft of one bag should not take both. A spouse who can open a drawer you both know about is a relationship decision — next lessons. A group chat is not a location. It is a broadcast.

Steel is for when fire is a real risk and the amount justifies it. Paper is enough for the drill. Do the drill before you shop for plates.

NOTE
Never put a seed in the same envelope as a full identity dump “for convenience.” Theft of that envelope is identity plus vault. Never run the restore half of the drill on a café PC or on a remote-desktop session. Academy staff will not watch you restore “to grade the lab.”
ENDNOTE


## What “second view” is allowed to be

A second user account on your phone. A spare phone that is yours, updated, official app. A hardware device restoring from the paper you wrote — only if that device was initialized by you and is not a pre-seeded marketplace unit.

What it is not: an internet café, a phone repair counter, a friend’s phone, a Zoom share, an academy “restore portal.” If the only way to restore is one of those, you do not restore. You paper-drill and you wait for a clean spare. The coins can wait. The leak cannot be un-done.


## Label the paper without decorating it

A small note “practice / BSC / 2026” on the same sheet is useful so a future you does not mix two vaults. A doodle, a gold sticker, or a photo of the sheet for “the aesthetic” is how backups become content. Boring paper in a boring place is the drill. If you cannot stand boring, you are not drilling — you are performing.

If the tiny receive never arrives, you still have a restore proof of the address. Funding can wait. The restore is the product of this lesson, not the balance.

## What this lesson is for

You have a pass/fail drill. Next: sharing a household without sharing a seed — spouses, shops, and the difference between a watcher and a signer.

## Say this out loud

- A backup that was never restored is a rumour. Drill with tiny funds.
- Write, confirm, tiny receive, restore, store, one human plan.
- Two copies of the same ordered list beat one clever hiding place and beat two different encodings.
- Café restore is a leak. Photo restore is a leak. Group-chat restore is a leak.
- If you cannot pass the drill, do not store rent in that vault.

Next: sharing a household without sharing a seed.

lessons.title: Sharing a household without sharing a seed
lessons.content:
# Sharing a household without sharing a seed

A household is not one brain. Self-custody that assumes one brain will fail at the first hospital, the first shop shift, or the first argument.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to name ways two adults can receive, watch, and (if they truly want) spend, without pasting twelve words into a family WhatsApp.

## Watch versus spend versus custody of the paper

**Watch-only** on a shop tablet: the tablet shows incoming BNB or USDT. It cannot spend. The seed is not on the stall. This is how a shop shares a view without sharing a vault.

**Two wallets:** each adult has their own seed, their own paper, their own practice. They send to each other as they would send to a client — full sentence, tiny test. This is the default this academy likes. Boring. Clear. When one phone dies, the other person is not holding a hostage combination.

**One vault, two signers** (more than one key required) is an advanced design. It is real. It is easy to botch. It is not Basic homework. If a YouTube video says “just use a multisig,” you are allowed to say “later.”

**One vault, shared seed** is the common disaster: both phones have the words, or one notes app is shared, or the paper sits in a drawer every cousin knows. You have doubled the leak surface. You have also doubled the chance of a quiet send during a fight. If you choose this, you are choosing a joint account without a bank referee. Name it that way.

TABLE
Setup | Who can see | Who can spend | Typical fail
Watch-only tablet | Shop / spouse | Nobody on that tablet | Seed later imported “so we can refund”
Two wallets, two seeds | Each their own | Each their own | Paying the wrong of the two doors
One seed on two phones | Both | Both, from either phone | One leak empties both views
Paper in a known drawer | Anyone who opens it | Anyone who restores | Relatives, theft, a teenager
Custodial joint exchange | Both logins if you set it so | Company can freeze | IOU, not keys — sometimes simpler
ENDTABLE

**Worked scenario.** Sam and her husband run a stall. They want to take BEP-20 USDT.

1. They create **one** receiving wallet on Sam's official app. They write the seed properly. They do not put it in the couple chat.
2. They set a cheap tablet to **watch-only** on that address. Customers can see a tick when BscScan moves. The tablet cannot send.
3. Refunds, if any, wait until Sam is on her own phone, reading ends, with a gas reserve. They do not import the seed onto the tablet “just this once.”
4. The husband’s personal funds live on a **different** seed. Stall money and rent money are different objects if they want them to be.
5. If they later want him to spend stall funds without her phone, they are choosing either a second stall wallet they fund on purpose, or a shared-seed risk they can name. They do not pretend WhatsApp is a signer policy.

DIAGRAM
Stall receive address
      |
      +--> Sam's phone (keys)  -->  can spend
      +--> tablet watch-only   -->  can see, cannot spend
      +--> BscScan bookmark    -->  book

Household personal
      |
      +--> Sam's second seed (optional)
      +--> husband’s seed
      +--> no group-chat backup
ENDDIAGRAM

## Children, cousins, and “help me restore”

Do not let a helpful teenager finish the restore quiz. Do not dictate words to a cousin on a call. Do not share a screen on video while the words are visible. Household help is how seeds travel. If someone must help with a phone problem, they help with the app install — official store — not with the paper.

A shared Android backup of a wallet app can copy keys to a cloud. Check what the phone backs up before you call a setup “hers only.” If you do not know, assume hot.

NOTE
A family WhatsApp group is not a vault, not an inheritance plan, and not a shop policy. If you need both adults to spend, say so and pick a design. If you need both adults to see, use watch-only. Do not paste twelve words into the chat because it feels like teamwork.
ENDNOTE


## Money fights are not a dApp setting

If a couple cannot agree who may spend stall funds, a shared seed will not heal that. It will make the fight faster. Use two wallets and a rule you can say: “stall USDT sits on Sam's practice-sized hot wallet, watch-only on the tablet, surplus goes to an exchange IOU / a colder wallet once a week.” Rules are adult. Shared phrases in chat are not.

If you hire a shop assistant, they get a watch-only view or a separate till wallet you fund with a ceiling, not the family vault. Staff turnover is a leak event.


## Guests on the Wi-Fi are not co-signers

A visiting cousin on the shop tablet should see a watch-only view, not a signer. Log out of anything that can spend before you hand a device to a guest. A fingerprint registered for “convenience” on a shared phone is a spender. Name it.

## What this lesson is for

You can separate seeing from spending in a house or a stall. Next: death, family, and inheritance without folklore — the plan that is not a Telegram admin.

## Say this out loud

- Watch-only shares a view. It does not share a seed. Do not “upgrade” a tablet by importing words.
- Two adults, two seeds is the boring default. Sending between them uses the same receive ritual as a client.
- One seed on two phones doubles the leak and doubles the quiet send.
- Shop QR and shop seed are different objects. The counter shows a door. The paper stays off the stall.
- Help with an app install, not with the paper. Video calls and group chats are cameras.

Next: death, family, and inheritance without folklore.

lessons.title: Death, family, and inheritance without folklore
lessons.content:
# Death, family, and inheritance without folklore

If nobody can find the words, the coins are a monument. If everybody can find the words, the coins are a fight.

By the end of this lesson you should refuse two folk stories: “they will figure it out from my phone PIN,” and “I’ll just put the twelve words in the family group so nobody is left out.” You should replace them with a plan you can say in one paragraph.

This academy does not write your will. It refuses to pretend self-custody is only a tech skill.

## What actually happens without a plan

A holder dies. The family has the phone PIN and the exchange password on a sticky note. The self-custody seed was only in the holder’s head, or only in a photo album nobody can unlock, or only on a hardware device whose PIN died with them.

The exchange IOU might be recoverable with documents, next-of-kin process, and time. That is a company-and-law story. The self-custody wallet is gone if the combination is gone. Name which bucket each pile of value is in **before** it matters.

A hardware box without the PIN and without the paper is a brick. A paper without order is a puzzle. A passphrase nobody else knows is a second brick. Complexity you cannot explain to a tired relative is not a gift.

TABLE
Bucket | What the family needs | What will not work
Custodial exchange / fintech | Legal process, logins if any, the company’s rules | A seed they do not have; a Telegram “recovery agent”
Self-custody software | The ordered words (and passphrase if any) | Phone PIN alone; IMEI; email password alone
Hardware | Device PIN **or** the seed backup; preferably the backup | A marketplace clone; a firmware from a helper
Watch-only tablet | Nothing to spend | Importing a guessed seed
ENDTABLE

**Worked scenario.** A holder in the family kept Crystal Stones and BNB on a phone wallet, seed in his head “because paper can be stolen,” exchange USDT in an example centralised exchange with a written password.

1. The exchange pile is an IOU. A spouse with documents may have a path. It will be slow. It is not nothing.
2. The phone wallet is a monument. PIN opens furniture. It does not reprint a seed that never existed on paper.
3. A helper on Facebook offers to recover the seed from the dead phone for a fee, leftover funds first. That is a second theft. This academy will not teach you to pay that person.
4. The adult plan, written while alive: paper or steel in a known place, a sealed letter, a lawyer or a trusted person, and a list of **which** buckets exist (exchange names, chain, that a BEP-20 token might need to be added by contract to be seen — 0xe252FCb1Aa2E0876E9B5f3eD1e15B9b4d11A0b00 as verify-only).
5. The letter should not sit in the same envelope as every identity photocopy if theft of that envelope would be total. Tradeoffs are allowed. Silence is not a plan.

DIAGRAM
Alive, today
   --> list buckets (IOU vs keys)
   --> drill the backup
   --> one paragraph for a human
   --> store paper so that human can find it without a group chat

Death with no paragraph
   --> PIN and email are not a seed
   --> helpers appear
   --> keys-bucket is gone; IOU-bucket is a queue
ENDDIAGRAM

## Split knowledge is advanced and easy to botch

Some people split: one person has the location of the paper, another has a passphrase. That can work. It can also guarantee that after a funeral nobody can open anything. If you cannot run the backup drill with your own brain, do not design a two-person puzzle.

A sealed letter with a lawyer or a trusted person is ordinary adult behaviour in other parts of life. Use it if it fits your legal world. This course will not pretend it is the same in every country. It will pretend that WhatsApp is not a will.

NOTE
Never put a seed in the same envelope as a full identity dump “for convenience” unless you have accepted that theft of that envelope is identity plus vault. Never send leftover funds to a stranger who promises to recover a dead relative’s wallet. We will not give that advice in a prettier costume.
ENDNOTE


## What to put in the paragraph

Which buckets exist (exchange names, self-custody, hardware). Where the paper is, in language a tired person can follow. That BNB Smart Chain is chain id 56 and BscScan is the book. That a BEP-20 token may need adding by contract to be seen — and the Crystal Stones verify string if that token is in the pile. That passphrase is off, or the exact passphrase location if you defied the default. That nobody should pay a Facebook recovery agent.

Do not put the raw seed in a WhatsApp draft of that paragraph. The paragraph points. The paper sits. Two objects.


## Law still applies

Self-custody does not delete tax, marriage, or probate law in your country. It only deletes the help desk. A plan that fights your law is a future court and a present leak. Use a professional if the amount would justify one. This academy will not draft documents. It will tell you that a group chat is not a professional.

## What this lesson is for

You can speak inheritance without folklore. Next: the self-custody checklist you will reuse on every send, including the phrases that mean close the app.

## Say this out loud

- Phone PIN is not a seed. Email is not a seed. A dead hardware box without paper is a brick.
- Name which funds are IOUs and which are keys before it matters. The playbooks differ.
- A paragraph for a human beats a group chat. Split puzzles are advanced.
- Recovery agents who want leftover funds first are thieves.
- Complexity the family cannot run is not love. It is a monument.

Next: the self-custody checklist.

lessons.title: The self-custody checklist
lessons.content:
# The self-custody checklist

Print this in your head. Use it before any amount that would annoy you to lose.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to run the list without looking, and you should recognise the phrases that mean close the app, hang up, and go back to a bookmark.

## Before you create

- Official app or hardware from the maker. Trust Wallet and MetaMask are examples of wallet apps, not ads. Ledger and Trezor are examples of hardware, not ads.
- Pen and paper ready. Numbered lines. No screenshots.
- No café generator, no Telegram bot, no “academy portal.”

## After you create

- Words written and confirmed in order.
- Restore proved with zero funds or a tiny practice amount.
- Paper not in the cloud, not in chat, not in the phone case.

## Before you receive

- Network is the one the sender will use. For this academy’s token path: BNB Smart Chain, BEP-20, chain id 56.
- Address from your receive screen, not from a DM PDF.
- You can explain asset + network + standard. Memo/tag only if a CEX deposit page truly requires it.

## Before you send

- Dropdown is the right book.
- First/last 6 match. Address book names are stickers.
- Tiny test if it matters. Explorer row before remainder.
- BNB reserved for gas. No Max on BNB if tokens still need a courier.
- No Approve on a mystery site. Connect is not Approve. Approve is not Send.

## If something feels like support

- Academy, wallet brands, exchanges, the checkout processor, Crystal Stones “admins” will not DM you for a seed, a private key, 2FA, or remote desktop.
- Hang up. Open the real site from a bookmark.
- “Validate with your seed,” “pay gas to unlock,” “limited airdrop, approve now,” “send USDT, any network is fine” — close.

TABLE
Phrase | Action | Object they want
“Validate with your seed” | Close | The vault
“Pay gas to this address to unlock” | Close | Your BNB, then your tokens
“Limited airdrop, approve now” | Close | Unlimited allowance
“Send USDT, any network is fine” | Close | A mix-up they will not refund
“Install this APK / this firmware” | Close | A clone of the app or the device
“Share screen, I’ll set gwei” | Close | The pen while you watch
ENDTABLE

You now have a key-manager mental model, a seed practice, a receive/send ritual, a leak playbook, and a household paragraph. The next module is a lab: official stores only, practice amounts only, no seed typed into a website. The next Basic course after this one — Exchanges & Your First Buy — is about the **on-ramp**: KYC, order books, and withdrawals onto the rails you just learned.

DIAGRAM
Create official --> paper --> restore proof
        |
        v
Receive: network + your screen + test + explorer
        |
        v
Send: dropdown + ends + gas reserve + sheet named out loud
        |
        v
Support phrases --> close --> bookmark

Empty and competent beats funded and confused.
ENDDIAGRAM

**Worked scenario.** A student finishes this checklist out loud, then a chat shouts that Crystal Stones will “list tomorrow” and they must Approve a pool.

1. They name the object: this is Approve, not a send they started, not a lesson.
2. They do not buy because a chat shouted. This academy still does not tell them to buy.
3. They may add the published contract as a view: 0xe252FCb1Aa2E0876E9B5f3eD1e15B9b4d11A0b00 on BSC. Viewing is not investing.
4. They keep the paper where the drill put it. They do not photograph it to “show they are ready.”
5. They go to Module 6’s lab with an amount they can lose, or with an empty wallet and a paper drill only.

NOTE
Still not a buy order for Crystal Stones. You can add the contract to view. You can finish this course with an empty wallet. Empty and competent beats funded and confused. Paid-track checkout, when you meet it, is USDT on BNB Smart Chain (BEP-20) through academy checkout — not this token, not a chat 0x.
ENDNOTE


## After a send, before you brag

- Explorer row matches the job you meant.
- You still have BNB for the next fee.
- You did not screenshot the seed in celebration.
- You did not paste the seed into a “certificate.”
- You named whether this pile is still an IOU on an exchange or keys you hold.

## Weekly five-minute hygiene

Once a week is enough for a beginner: confirm the paper is where you left it; confirm the app is still the official publisher; confirm you did not connect a mystery site; confirm BscScan still matches the screen for an address you care about. Hygiene is dull. Dull is the point.

If you hold a view of Crystal Stones, confirm the contract has not been replaced in your wallet’s token list by a lookalike. The published string remains 0xe252FCb1Aa2E0876E9B5f3eD1e15B9b4d11A0b00. A new logo in the list is not a new truth.


## One line you can text a friend

“Coins are on the chain, the app is a window, the paper is the combination, BNB pays BSC gas, USDT is not USDT on every road, Approve is a gun, support never needs the words.” If they want more, they can take this course. If a stranger wants more — the words, the screen, the 2FA — they are not your friend.

## What this lesson is for

The list is the product. Take the quiz. Then the lab: set up without risking rent.

## Say this out loud

- Official create, paper backup, proved restore. Cloud copies poison the setup.
- Full sentence: asset, network, standard, address. Test, explorer, gas reserve.
- Name the sheet: Connect, Sign, Send, Approve. If you cannot name it, reject it.
- Support never needs the words, the key, the 2FA, or the desktop.
- Empty and competent beats funded and confused.

Take the quiz. Then the lab — official stores, practice amounts, no seed on a website.

lessons.title: Choosing an official wallet app without downloading a clone
lessons.content:
# Choosing an official wallet app without downloading a clone

This module is a lab. You will not be asked to buy Crystal Stones. You will not be asked to type a seed into a website. You will use official stores, practice amounts you can lose, and BscScan as the book.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to install an example wallet app from a source you can defend, and you should recognise clone tells: a slightly wrong publisher, an APK from a group chat, a “Crystal Stones official wallet” that is not a wallet this academy ships.

## Official store means the publisher, not the icon

Trust Wallet and MetaMask are **examples of wallet apps**. Pick one you will actually keep updated, or pick a hardware companion only if you already own a device from the maker. This academy does not need a brand loyalty oath.

On a phone, use the App Store or Google Play. Tap the publisher name. Compare it to the publisher named on the product’s own website that **you typed**, not a sponsored first result. Clone apps copy icons, screenshots, and even review counts. They exist to catch the restore of a seed.

Do not sideload an APK from Telegram, WhatsApp, or a “faster download” site. Do not let a cousin install it for you from their files app. If a shop assistant offers a phone “already set up for crypto,” treat the wallet as hostile until you uninstall and reinstall from the official store, then create a **new** seed — the preinstalled one is not yours.

On a computer, MetaMask-as-example is a browser extension from the official extension store plus a publisher check. Fake extensions live in ads. Bookmark the real docs. Do not install from a banner that followed you after a search for Crystal Stones.

TABLE
Source | Beginner verdict | Why
App Store / Play, publisher matched to the typed official site | OK for this lab | Still not an endorsement
Official hardware shop, sealed, you initialize | OK if you already chose hardware | Tamper risk if used or pre-seeded
APK / “mod” / Telegram file | No | Clone harvester
Shop phone with wallet preinstalled | No until you wipe and reinstall | Seed may already be known
Sponsored “MetaMask download” ad | No | Classic clone path
“Crystal Stones Academy wallet” APK | No | We do not ship a custodial app that needs your seed
ENDTABLE

**Worked scenario.** A student searches “Trust Wallet APK” because Play Store is slow.

1. The first download button is an ad. The APK asks for restore on first open.
2. If they restore a funded seed, the clone has the combination. If they create a new seed inside the clone, the clone may still exfiltrate it.
3. The adult path: wait for Play or App Store. Match publisher. Create later, on that official binary.
4. They do not “test the APK with a dummy seed” on the same phone they will later fund. Dummy seeds become habits.
5. If they already installed a clone, they do not type any real seed into it. Uninstall. Official install. New words if anything was ever entered on the clone.

DIAGRAM
Typed official website --> publisher name
        |
        v
App Store / Play / official extension store
        |
        v
Publisher match --> install --> stop
        |
        x  ads, APK chats, preinstalled shop phones, “academy wallet”

You have an app. You do not yet have a vault. That is the next lesson.
ENDDIAGRAM

## What this academy will never send you

A download link in email. A QR to an APK. A “student edition” wallet. A request to enable remote desktop so we can install it. If our name is on those, it is a costume. Course progress does not live in your seed.

After install, do not create the wallet yet if the room is public. Pen, privacy, next lesson. If the app nags you to back up to iCloud, that nag is the Notes-app trap in a tuxedo. You will write paper.

NOTE
Crystal Stones Academy does not ship a wallet APK and will never ask you to install one to mark a lesson complete. Official stores only. If a mentor-shaped account sends a download, it is theft wearing a syllabus.
ENDNOTE


## Review scores are not a publisher

Clones buy reviews. A 4.8 star APK with 80,000 ratings can still be a harvester. Publisher match plus typed official site beats the score. If the store listing’s company name is a near-miss — one extra letter, a different country suffix — stop.

After install, before create: open the app’s settings and see whether it is begging for a seed import as the first screen. Create is the lab. Import is how clones eat old vaults. If you came here with a funded seed, you still create a new lab vault. You do not import rent into a fresh install as a test.


## After a clone scare

If you already typed a real seed into a clone, that is Module 2’s leak lesson, not a reinstall footnote. New official app. New words. Move what you can. Retire the old phrase. Reinstalling the real app and typing the same words again is how you feed the clone’s harvest to a second screen — the words are already burned.

## What this lesson is for

You have a clean binary, or you know how to get one. Next: create a new wallet and prove the backup — offline write, then restore to a second profile if possible, or a paper drill.

## Say this out loud

- Official store plus matched publisher. Icons are not proof. Ads are not stores.
- No APK from chat, no preinstalled shop wallet, no academy-branded seed app.
- A clone’s job is to watch you type words. Do not give it a funded seed or a “test” seed you later reuse.
- Hardware, if you use it, comes from the maker and is initialized by you.
- Progress in this course does not require a special wallet build.

Next: creating a new wallet and proving the backup.

lessons.title: Creating a new wallet and proving the backup
lessons.content:
# Creating a new wallet and proving the backup

Create on the official app you just installed, or on a hardware screen if that is your signer. Write paper. Prove restore. Do not fund rent.

By the end of this lesson you should have numbered words on paper and evidence that those words open the same addresses — via the app’s confirmation quiz plus a restore to a second profile if you can do it safely, or a strict paper drill if you cannot.

## Create, write, confirm

1. Be in a private place. No video call. No shop CCTV over your shoulder if you can avoid it. Airplane mode is optional and fine.
2. Tap Create, not Import, unless you are restoring a seed you already own. This lab is a **new** vault.
3. When 12 or 24 words appear, write them in order on numbered lines. Block letters. No photo. No printer. No Notes app “until I get paper.”
4. Complete the app’s confirmation quiz from the paper, not from memory of the screen.
5. Leave the optional passphrase **off** unless you can teach Module 2’s passphrase lesson and store a second secret. This lab’s default is off.
6. Write the date and “practice wallet” on the paper if it helps you not mix it with a later vault. Do not write the words in a title of a cloud file.

If the app offers iCloud or Google backup of the seed, refuse. That is a hot copy. You are practising self-custody, not a new kind of exchange.

## Prove the backup

The in-app quiz is necessary and not sufficient. People tap the quiz while the words are still on the other half of the screen.

If the app allows a second profile, or you have a spare device that is yours, restore there from paper and check that the **address** matches the first view. Then remove the spare restore if it lives on a noisier device than you want. Each extra live copy is extra hot surface.

If you cannot restore on a second view without typing on a café PC, do a **paper drill**: cover the app, read the paper aloud privately, uncover, confirm every word. Then, later, when you have a clean spare, restore for real before the amount grows.

Never prove a backup by pasting words into a website “seed checker,” an academy lookalike, or a Discord bot.

TABLE
Proof | Counts? | Note
In-app word-order quiz | Partial | Necessary. Easy to cheat while the screen still shows words
Restore on a second profile / spare you own | Yes | Best lab. Remove extra live copies you do not want hot
Paper read-back, screen covered | Partial | Better than nothing when no spare exists
Website “validate seed” | No | Theft
Photo of the paper | No | Leak
ENDTABLE

**Worked scenario.** Maya creates a wallet on the official app, writes twelve words, then sees a banner: “Verify backup — paste your phrase to continue the Crystal Stones lesson.”

1. That banner is not this course. She closes it.
2. She finishes the in-app quiz from paper.
3. She uses Android’s second user / a spare old phone of hers to restore. The 0x matches. She does not leave the spare signed-in in a shared house if that house is leaky.
4. She has proved the backup with zero funds. She is allowed to receive a practice amount next. She is not required to.
5. If the restore had shown a different 0x, she would not fund anything. She would check order, check passphrase-off, check she did not shuffle the paper.

DIAGRAM
Create on official app / hardware screen
        |
        v
Write numbered paper (no photo, no cloud)
        |
        v
In-app quiz from paper
        |
        v
Restore proof (second profile or strict paper drill)
        |
        v
Zero funds still OK — next lesson is a tiny receive, not rent

Website seed paste = stop. Wrong course. Theft.
ENDDIAGRAM

## One lab wallet

Do not create five seeds “for practice.” You will mix papers. One practice vault, labelled, stored like the real thing, even if it will only ever hold a tiny BNB. Habits transfer. Sloppy practice becomes sloppy funded.

If you already had a funded wallet, do **not** type that seed into this lab’s second profile as a demo. The lab is a new phrase. Keep old phrases off noisy extra devices.

NOTE
Crystal Stones Academy will never require you to paste words into our site to mark this lesson complete. If a page says it is required, it is not us. Prove the backup on the official app, on paper, optionally on a spare you own.
ENDNOTE


## If the words look “too common”

BIP-39 words are ordinary. “Apple” does not mean the vault is weak. Do not swap a word for a synonym. Do not add a 13th word as a joke. Do not skip a word that appeared twice — duplicates can happen. Copy the screen. The next lesson is receive, not poetry.

If you lose the paper before the restore proof, you do not hunt in the app’s settings for a “show seed” while sitting on a bus. You wait until you are private, you write again if the app will still show the phrase (some will, some will not after you skip), or you abandon that empty vault and create a new one. Empty is the time to be ruthless. Funded is too late.

## What this lesson is for

You have a proven empty vault, or you know exactly which proof you still owe yourself. Next: first receive of a practice amount on BSC — tiny, right network, explorer.

## Say this out loud

- Create, not import, for this lab. Write numbered paper. Passphrase off unless you can teach it.
- Refuse cloud backup of the seed. That is a hot copy.
- Prove restore on a spare you own, or do a strict paper drill. Websites do not validate seeds.
- One practice vault. Do not mix papers. Do not demo with a funded seed on a noisy extra device.
- Matching 0x after restore is the proof. Feelings are not.

Next: first receive of a practice amount on BNB Smart Chain.

lessons.title: First receive of a practice amount on BSC
lessons.content:
# First receive of a practice amount on BSC

Now the door. A tiny amount. The right book. An explorer row. Not rent.

By the end of this lesson you should have received a practice amount of **BNB** (native gas coin) on **BNB Smart Chain**, or you should have walked the ritual on paper if you are not moving value yet. BNB is the courier. Tokens wait until you can pay the courier.

This academy does not tell you where you must obtain BNB. An example centralised exchange, a friend who already holds it, a P2P desk you already trust — those are on-ramps. The next Basic course treats on-ramps in full. Today: if value moves, it moves as a test you can lose, to an address you control, on chain id 56.

## The receive ritual, as a lab

1. Open your official wallet. Network = BNB Smart Chain. If you must add the network, you want chain id **56** and a reputable RPC, not a random pasted RPC from a chat.
2. Tap Receive. Copy the 0x from that screen. Check first 6 and last 6.
3. From the sending side — exchange withdrawal or a friend’s wallet — choose **BNB** on **BNB Smart Chain**, not BNB on the wrong product, not a token named BNB, not Ethereum.
4. Send a tiny amount. Wait. Do not nag the sender for a screenshot as proof.
5. Open BscScan from a bookmark. Paste **your** address. See the incoming BNB. That row is the lab pass.
6. If the wallet screen lags, believe the explorer. Delayed RPC is not theft. Do not send a second test because the icon is slow.

If you cannot move value this week, still do steps 1–2 and write your first 6 and last 6 in a private place that is **not** the seed paper. Knowing your door is part of the lab. Funding is optional. Competence is not.

TABLE
Sender choice | What to select | Lab fail
Exchange withdrawal | BNB, BEP-20/BSC network, your 0x, no invented memo unless the page requires one | TRC-20, ERC-20, or a memo meant for someone else’s product
Friend’s wallet | Their dropdown = BSC, asset = BNB, ends match | They send a token named BNB on another chain
You, from another of your wallets | Same full sentence | Max-sending all BNB from a wallet that still holds tokens
ENDTABLE

**Worked scenario.** Yusuf withdraws “BNB” from an example exchange and picks a network that is not BNB Smart Chain.

1. The exchange shows success. His BSC wallet does not move. BscScan on chain id 56 shows nothing.
2. He does not paste the seed into a recovery bot. He reads the withdrawal record: which network did the exchange send on?
3. Rescue, if any, is an exchange support story — maybe, maybe not. This lab prefers not needing rescue: pick BSC, tiny amount, explorer, then (only if you want) a little more for later gas.
4. He tries again, tiny, on BSC. BscScan shows the row. The wallet catches up. Lab pass.
5. He leaves that BNB as a gas reserve for the next two lessons. He does not swap it into a mystery token.

DIAGRAM
Your receive screen (BSC)
        |
        v
Tiny BNB from a venue you chose
        |
        v
BscScan row on YOUR address
        |
        v
Wallet screen may lag  -->  wait, do not double-send

Wrong network / wrong asset / wrong door = different book. Do not “try all networks” with rent.
ENDDIAGRAM

## How much is a practice amount

An amount whose disappearance would annoy you for an hour, not a month. If you do not have a number like that, skip funding. Watch-only labs still teach the dropdown. Empty and competent remains the motto.

Do not ask a stranger in a Crystal Stones group to “send me gas.” That invitation is how hunters find hungry addresses. Do not post your 0x under “first BNB please.” Dust and drainers follow.

NOTE
Practice with amounts you can lose. Prefer a test-send first. This academy will not reimburse a wrong-network withdrawal, will not send you gas, and will not ask you to receive Crystal Stones to pass the lab. BNB on BSC is the courier for later token views and a tiny self-send.
ENDNOTE


## Adding BSC if the app is blank

Some example apps, especially browser wallets, start on Ethereum. Adding BNB Smart Chain means chain id 56, symbol BNB, a public RPC you got from documentation you typed, not from a DM. A wrong RPC can be a delayed helper or a malicious helper. If the app offers an official “add BNB Smart Chain” switch, prefer that to a stranger’s pasted JSON.

Then receive. Then explorer. Then you may add a token view in the next lesson. Order matters: courier first, costume jewellery second.


## What the explorer row must show

Your address as the destination. BNB as the asset for this lab. Status success. The sending address can be an exchange hot wallet — that is normal. You are not looking for your name. You are looking for the door and the asset.

If you see a token transfer instead of BNB, you received a different object. Do not try to “convert it on a pop-up.” Note it, ignore mystery tokens, and do a BNB test if you still need the courier.

## What this lesson is for

You can receive BNB on the right book, or you can honestly postpone funding. Next: add Crystal Stones by contract as verify-only, and read the token on BscScan — still not a buy.

## Say this out loud

- Receive from your BSC screen. Chain id 56. Copy, check ends, tiny BNB, explorer row.
- Exchange dropdowns are network selectors too. BNB on the wrong road is the wrong object.
- Delayed wallet screens are not a dare to send twice. BscScan is the book.
- Do not beg strangers for gas. Do not post your address in a hunting ground.
- Funding is optional. The ritual is not.

Next: adding Crystal Stones by contract (verify, not buy) and reading the token on BscScan.

lessons.title: Adding Crystal Stones by contract (verify, not buy) and reading the token on BscScan
lessons.content:
# Adding Crystal Stones by contract (verify, not buy) and reading the token on BscScan

Adding a token is a view. BscScan is the book. Neither is a purchase.

By the end of this lesson you should have the published Crystal Stones contract in your wallet on BNB Smart Chain **or** you should have opened that contract on BscScan and read it like an adult. You should not have Approved anything. You should not have sent BNB to the contract “to activate.”

The public contract, as the project publishes it, is:

0xe252FCb1Aa2E0876E9B5f3eD1e15B9b4d11A0b00

Treat that as a **reference to verify**. This academy will not tell you to buy. Crystal Stones’ RWA story is their claim to verify elsewhere. This lab verifies **which program** you are looking at.

## On BscScan

1. Open BscScan from your bookmark. Confirm you are on the BSC explorer, not a fake.
2. Paste 0xe252FCb1Aa2E0876E9B5f3eD1e15B9b4d11A0b00.
3. You should land on a **token contract** page: a program, not a person’s empty wallet story. Note the name, the symbol, the decimals if shown, the contract address again — first 6 and last 6, then more of the middle.
4. Open your own address in another tab. If you hold none, you hold none. The holders list does not owe you a row.
5. If a second token named Crystal Stones appears on your address from an airdrop, compare **its** contract to the published one. Mismatch means clone. Do not tap Claim.

## In the wallet

1. Network is BNB Smart Chain.
2. Add custom token. Paste the published contract. The app should fill a name and symbol from the chain. If it asks you to Approve, you are not adding a view. Reject.
3. A zero balance is a successful add. A non-zero balance means that address already held some — still not a lesson to buy more.
4. Do not add a token from a pop-up that said “you received Crystal Stones.” Add from the published string you typed yourself.

TABLE
Lab move | Pass | Fail
Paste published contract on BscScan | Token page, address matches | Random Google clone, or a phishing explorer
Add token in wallet on BSC | View appears, no Approve sheet | Approve, WalletConnect from a DM, send BNB to contract
Ignore mystery airdrop | Hidden or leftover, not tapped | Claim site, unlimited allowance
Read your address on BscScan | You can find BNB and token tabs | Believing the wallet logo over the contract
ENDTABLE

**Worked scenario.** A student adds the token, sees 0, then a WhatsApp blast says “your academy allocation is waiting — connect to claim.”

1. This course did not allocate tokens. Connecting to claim is not a lab step.
2. They keep the view. They do not Approve. They do not sign a mystery message.
3. They reread the contract on BscScan and confirm it still matches 0xe252FCb1Aa2E0876E9B5f3eD1e15B9b4d11A0b00.
4. If they want a non-zero number one day, that is a later life decision this academy will not make for them. The lab is the match, not the balance.
5. They still have a BNB reserve from the previous lesson so that a later tiny send can pay a courier — not so they can feed a claim contract.

DIAGRAM
Typed contract 0xe252FCb1Aa2E0876E9B5f3eD1e15B9b4d11A0b00
        |
        +--> BscScan token page (book)
        +--> wallet custom token on BSC (view)
        |
        x  Approve
        x  send BNB to the contract
        x  claim sites
        x  the checkout processor mix-up (paid tracks, when live, are USDT BEP-20, not this token)

Name match is not contract match.
ENDDIAGRAM

## What you are not doing

You are not verifying a mine. You are not verifying a price. You are not paying tuition to this contract. Paid-track checkout, when live, is **USDT on BNB Smart Chain (BEP-20) through academy checkout**. Different rail. Different sentence. Do not send Crystal Stones to a USDT invoice, and do not send USDT to this contract.

If the wallet shows a different checksum casing, that can still be the same address. Compare without panicking. If the middle digits differ, it is not the same address.

NOTE
This lesson is verify-only. Not a buy order. Not a claim. Not a deposit address. Academy staff will not send a second “updated contract” in a DM. If the published contract ever changed, you would confirm from the same kinds of sources you used here — not from a blast.
ENDNOTE


## Two tabs, one string

Keep BscScan and the wallet add-token sheet open together. The string you paste in the wallet should be the string on the token page, not a string from a chat screenshot that “looks close.” Close is how clones live.

If your wallet already lists a Crystal Stones from an airdrop, hide it or ignore it. Add the published contract as a **new** custom token. Two rows with the same nickname can sit in one app. Only the contract tells you which row is the program this academy printed.

If you hold BNB from the previous lesson, do not swap it into the token as part of this lab. The lab is a view. Swapping is a later, optional life decision, and a sponsored swap is often a drainer.

## What this lesson is for

You can point at the program on the book. Next: a tiny send to yourself, then graduation — what you can do, what still waits for later courses.

## Say this out loud

- Adding Crystal Stones by contract is a view on BNB Smart Chain. It is not a purchase and not an Approve.
- The published contract to verify is 0xe252FCb1Aa2E0876E9B5f3eD1e15B9b4d11A0b00. Clone names do not count.
- BscScan is the book. A zero balance after adding can be an honest pass.
- Do not send BNB to the token contract to activate anything. Do not claim airdrops.
- Tuition, when it exists, is not this token and not this contract.

Next: a tiny send to yourself, then the graduation.

lessons.title: A tiny send to yourself, then the graduation: what you can do, what still waits for later courses
lessons.content:
# A tiny send to yourself, then the graduation

The last lab move is a send you cannot blame on a stranger: you to you, on BSC, tiny, then the explorer row. After that, we name what this course made you able to do, and what it did not.

By the end you should have either completed a self-send of practice BNB (or a tiny BEP-20 amount if you already held one), or you should be able to walk the steps without pretending a screenshot is a row.

## Tiny send to yourself

Why to yourself: the destination is a door you control. You still practise paste, ends, gas, and explorer. You still can fail — wrong network, no gas, clipboard malware swapping even your own address. Self-sends are not a joke. They catch sloppy hands before a client is involved.

1. If you have only one address, send a tiny BNB amount to that same address, or create a second account in the same app (same seed, different child address) and send there. A second account is not a second backup. It is a second door on the same tree — fine for this drill.
2. If you want a cleaner drill, send from the practice wallet to a **watch-only** view of the same address on BscScan only — still one signer. Do not invent a second seed for five minutes and lose the paper.
3. Network BSC. Asset BNB for the courier drill. Amount tiny. Check ends. Confirm on the sheet. Wait.
4. BscScan: from, to, amount, success. Your wallet may lag. The book wins.
5. Leave a gas reserve. Do not Max. If you also send a tiny token, you still pay BNB. Do not send Crystal Stones to yourself as a way of “buying a round trip.” Viewing was the previous lesson.

If you have no BNB, skip the live send. Recite the checklist out loud. You still graduate this course as a person who can refuse a seed phishing page. Funded theatre is not the certificate.

TABLE
You can do after this course | You still wait for
Name app, PIN, keys, chain as four objects | Exchange KYC, P2P, and first buy (next Basic course)
Create, paper, restore proof | Advanced revoke-allowance tools
Receive and send on BSC with a test and explorer | Complex dApp use, bridges, “best yield”
Add Crystal Stones as a verified view | Anyone’s permission to tell you to buy
Refuse seed / 2FA / remote-desktop theatre | Hardware shopping as a personality
Name Approve as a loaded gun | Safe unlimited on a venue you researched
A household paragraph | A lawyer-grade will this academy will not write
ENDTABLE

**Worked scenario.** Amaka sends 0.001 BNB to herself. Clipboard malware swaps the paste to a hunter. She checks last 6 on the confirm sheet, sees a mismatch, rejects.

1. That reject is a lab pass even if no send landed. The sheet did its job.
2. She copies again from the receive screen, checks ends, sends. BscScan shows her address on both from and to (or from account 0 to account 1).
3. She does not then Approve a “graduation dApp.” There is not one.
4. She puts the paper back. She does not post the tx hash in a public group with her life story. Explorers are public enough.
5. She can explain, out loud, that Crystal Stones Academy never needed her seed, that the contract 0xe252FCb1Aa2E0876E9B5f3eD1e15B9b4d11A0b00 was verify-only, and that the next course is on-ramps — not a command to empty an exchange today.

DIAGRAM
Practice BNB on BSC
        |
        v
Paste destination (self / account 1)
        |
        v
Check ends on THE SHEET
        |
        +--> mismatch --> reject --> copy again
        +--> match --> send --> BscScan row --> reserve left

Graduation is the ritual, not a token balance.
ENDDIAGRAM

## What still waits

Exchanges & Your First Buy: how an IOU on-ramp works, KYC, withdrawals that still need this course’s sentence (asset, network, standard). BNB Smart Chain for beginners: more of the chain itself. Crypto safety: drainers in more costumes. None of those courses will honestly ask for your seed either.

You may keep using a custodial exchange. You may never buy hardware. You may never hold Crystal Stones. You may hold a view of zero forever. The operating manual still applies whenever a key or an IOU is in play.

If this lab felt like a lot of paper for a tiny coin, that is the point. Self-custody is ops. People who skip ops become screenshots in group chats.

NOTE
Graduation is not a wallet-connect ceremony. We will not ask for a seed, a private key, 2FA, remote desktop, or an Approve to issue a certificate. Practice amounts only. Education only. Never a buy order.
ENDNOTE


## What you will still not do tomorrow

You will not import the lab seed into a second random app to “see Crystal Stones price.” You will not join a paid group that requires a screenshot of your phrase. You will not send leftover practice BNB to a recovery agent. You will not treat a certificate as a reason to Connect. The next course is the on-ramp. It still will not need the words.

## What this lesson is for

You have a complete Basic operating manual for wallets, keys, and self-custody on BNB Smart Chain. Take the quiz. Then go to the next course when you are ready — not when a chat is shouting.

## Say this out loud

- A tiny self-send practises paste, ends, gas, and explorer without a client in the story. The sheet can still save you from malware.
- Leave a BNB reserve. Do not Max. Do not Approve a graduation dApp. There is not one.
- This course made you able to name objects, back up a seed, receive and send on BSC, verify a contract, and refuse theatre.
- It did not tell you to buy Crystal Stones, empty an exchange, or worship a hardware brand.
- Academy staff still will never ask for the words. If someone does, they are not us.

Take the quiz. Then the next Basic course when you are ready — not when a chat is shouting.
